items.title: CGTN / Gande-1 01 — space-based optical tracking and impact-region imaging
items.source: CGTN (reporting Gande-1 01 / Aotian Technology / Liangxi Aerospace Technology Group)
items.evidence: CGTN reports that the Gande-1 01 commercial debris-monitoring satellite imaged the Falcon 9 upper stage approaching the Moon on 1 and 3 August and recorded images of the lunar region at the 5 August impact time from roughly 380,000 km. The page shows reported sensor imagery but provides no plate scale, cadence, astrometric residuals, radiometric calibration, raw files, or independently quantified impact signature.

items.title: NASA LRO/LROC — confirmed crater and calibrated NAC measurements
items.evidence: LRO’s Narrow Angle Camera acquired six post-impact images on 11–12 August and confirmed the crater at 19.4759°N, 266.7138°E, elevation 511 m, measuring 18 m diameter and less than 3 m deep; the imagery also resolves bright/dark ejecta and a V-shaped low-angle pattern. The page provides image IDs and viewing geometry, but no downloadable calibrated reflectance/photometric product or formal uncertainty bounds for the crater dimensions.

items.title: ESO Very Large Telescope / UVES — sodium and lithium spectroscopy
items.source: Associated Press (reporting Carl Schmidt / ESO VLT-UVES)
items.evidence: Boston University’s Carl Schmidt told AP that VLT/UVES detected sodium and lithium extending tens of kilometres for roughly five to ten minutes after impact. This is reported spectroscopic sensor evidence, but no ESO data release, reduced spectrum, observing log, or calibration product has yet been published; ingest the page as a vetted report, not as a released dataset.

items.title: KASA Danuri (KPLO/LUTI) — agency-released orbital before/after imaging
items.evidence: KASA’s official release publishes Danuri high-resolution LUTI imagery acquired immediately before and after the Falcon 9 impact, confirming the new surface disturbance at the predicted site. The release provides processed comparison imagery but no calibrated crater dimensions, ejecta-ray measurements, photometric product, or formal measurement uncertainties.

items.title: IAA-CSIC / MIDAS — time-resolved optical ejecta video
items.source: José María Madiedo / Instituto de Astrofísica de Andalucía (IAA-CSIC/MIDAS)
items.evidence: José María Madiedo reports that the IAA-CSIC team captured the Falcon 9 upper-stage lunar impact and released an 11-second preliminary video showing ejecta evolving beyond the lunar limb. This is direct optical sensor imagery, but the public clip remains uncalibrated: no plate scale, cadence, photometry, or kilometre conversion has been released.
